description: Somos un equipo de estudiantes de Ingeniería de Sistemas de Andahuaylas, apasionados por la tecnología, el espacio y la educación. Queremos crear un videojuego interactivo donde niños y jóvenes entrenen como astronautas, resuelvan misiones y tomen decisiones sobre energía, recursos y seguridad en la Luna o Marte, usando información de la NASA. Buscamos integrantes con interés en programación, videojuegos, diseño UI/UX, ilustración, ciencia y educación. ¡Únete a nuestra misión!
summary:
A space mission can fail before launch—not because its scientific goal is wrong, but because its design cannot balance competing constraints.

**SELENE-01: Architects of Space** transforms this systems-engineering challenge into an interactive 3D educational game. Players explore a space center, define a lunar science objective, and design ODYSSEY, a fictional uncrewed orbiter investigating the Moon's south pole.

Every decision has consequences. Choosing scientific instruments, orbital configurations, launch vehicles, and mission duration affects mass, power, data capacity, and budget. Players must validate their designs, experience a simulated launch, manage orbital operations, and analyze their results before redesigning their mission.

Guided by TARS, a robotic companion connecting gameplay to publicly available NASA scientific resources, students explore the reasoning behind real mission-design challenges.

Developed by six Systems Engineering students from Peru, SELENE-01 aims to make space engineering more accessible through experimentation, critical thinking, and learning from failure.

**Our vision: make the complexity of space exploration something students can experience, question, and understand.**
details:
SELENE-01 — Project Details

The Challenge

Designing a space mission requires more than selecting a spacecraft or a scientific instrument. Engineers must balance scientific objectives with interconnected constraints such as mass, available power, data transmission, mission duration, launch capabilities, and budget.

These trade-offs are difficult to experience through traditional classroom explanations alone.

SELENE-01 addresses this educational challenge by allowing students to experiment with mission-design decisions in an interactive environment where choices produce visible consequences.

Our Solution

SELENE-01: Architects of Space is a browser-based, three-dimensional educational adventure developed by a team of six Systems Engineering students from Peru.

The central mission challenges players to design ODYSSEY, a fictional uncrewed scientific orbiter intended to study the Moon's south polar region.

Players begin by exploring an interactive space center, where they receive scientific objectives and visit specialized stations for research, engineering, communications, and launch preparation.

The experience combines exploration, storytelling, engineering decisions, resource management, and scientific explanations.

How It Works

Players select a lunar science objective, assemble their spacecraft, choose instruments and supporting systems, and configure the orbit, launch vehicle, and mission duration.

Each configuration is evaluated against educational constraints involving mass, power, data transmission, and budget.

If the design exceeds its limits, players must reconsider their choices before proceeding.

Once validated, the spacecraft can enter a simulated launch sequence. Players then make orbital operation decisions involving scientific observation, energy conservation, and data transmission.

The mission concludes with a report explaining the simulated results and the consequences of the player's decisions. Players can redesign their spacecraft and explore alternative outcomes.

Integration of NASA Resources

SELENE-01 connects its educational experience to publicly available NASA scientific resources.

Our references include NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter mission, lunar water and ice research, Mini-RF radar investigations, and NASA's systems engineering principles.

TARS, our interactive robotic companion, guides players through selected scientific explanations and provides links to NASA resources. The project also supports optional searches through NASA's Image and Video Library.

NASA's research provides scientific context; the spacecraft specifications, mission budgets, resource values, and simulation outcomes are hypothetical educational models. SELENE-01 is not a flight-qualified engineering simulator.

Technology and Creativity

The prototype was developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber, and Drei, with 3D assets integrated through Blender-compatible GLB models.

Its stylized illustrated world, interactive facilities, animated spacecraft, contextual robotic guide, and mission-validation mechanics bring together game development and introductory systems engineering.

Rather than providing a single predetermined solution, the game encourages players to compare alternatives, experience constraints, and learn through iteration.

Educational Impact

SELENE-01 is designed for students, aspiring engineers, and learners interested in space exploration.

Its intended educational outcomes include strengthening systems thinking, scientific reasoning, resource awareness, and understanding of engineering trade-offs.

The current prototype demonstrates an interactive mission-design workflow. Future development will focus on greater scientific fidelity, additional mission scenarios, accessibility, and structured educational testing.

Our goal is to make the reasoning behind space missions understandable—not only through explanation, but through experience.
